correctness.rationale: For every 2<=p<=q, the selected-edge graph in K_{p,q} has an acyclic line graph exactly when it is a linear forest. Maximality forces saturation of all p-side vertices when p<q and a spanning alternating Hamilton path when p=q; the respective uniform sizes are 2p and 2p-1. Explicit alternating-path enumeration gives the two-sort exponential formula and component-refined maximum count. Complete independent direct adjacency subset checks for ten boards including 4x4 (104290 total subsets) reproduce all coefficients and all inclusion-maximal counts; finite tests do not substitute for the infinite proof. Principal risks: graph-to-line-graph cycle argument and maximality under addition are both fully justified in the proof.

originality.rationale: The direct 2021 well-f-coveredness source treats K_{p,q} itself in Corollary 6.16, not L(K_{p,q}); its complete-bipartite classification does not imply the rook-graph all-maximal property. The known well-coveredness of rook graphs addresses maximal independent sets only. Actual published-finding corpus and web searches of equivalent line-graph, maximal linear forest, and feedback vertex set formulations produced no covering claim. The possible existence of an unindexed exact linear-forest enumeration is acknowledged as residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A not-indexed or differently-termed source on maximal edge-disjoint alternating path forests in K_{p,q} might imply the all-maximal characterization.
The labeled-path exponential formula is a natural application of the classical exponential formula; originality does not extend to that general principle.
Other same-graph papers identified only by abstract or search excerpt were not declared wholly not covering.

value.rationale: Well-f-coveredness is a motivated structural question for maximal induced forests and complements to minimal feedback vertex sets; for all p,q this theorem proves the strong property that every inclusion-minimal feedback vertex set is minimum. It also provides the complete labeled size distribution and component-resolved counts, showing an exact component spectrum that varies with the aspect ratio q/p. These results are not simply the known well-coveredness of rook graphs or a minor extremal bound; they solve a coherent infinite-family classification.
